"We couldn't wish for a more approachable professional team of people"
South Moreton Parent
“The World for our Children, Our Children for the World” demonstrates our commitment to providing the very best for each and every one of our pupils, so that they can begin to carve their journey into the future with a solid foundation of skills and knowledge.
We focus our developments as a community around three main elements: academic excellence, resilience and wellbeing, and global citizenship. The roots of our work are evident across our happy school.
I would be delighted to show you around our wonderful school so you can see for yourself, and to help you in your decision to bring your child to join us. Please telephone or email the School Office to arrange an appointment.
Mrs Cheryl Sánchez, Headteacher.

pageCache.text:
Special educational needs and disability provision
South Moreton Primary School is an inclusive school, supporting children with a wide range of learning needs and disabilities. The documents below outline South Moreton's approach to SEND provision. Please do not hesitate to contact the school if you require further information.
"There has been such high support for my child which has really built confidence and self-worth."
South Moreton Parent
We also set out how the school enables pupils with special needs and disabilities to participate in all aspects of school life through our Accessibility Plan on our Policies page.
"It's a family friendly feel. The teachers know my child well and respond to his needs."
South Moreton Parent

pageCache.pageTitle: South Moreton Primary School - Personal Development at South Moreton
pageCache.text:
Personal Development at South Moreton
We wish for children to leave South Moreton with the confidence, resilience and self-identity to make their way in the world as successful global citizens.
Our Personal Development Curriculum is carefully planned and structured to ensure a wide, rich set of experiences to develop knowledge, talent and interests.
Take a look below at the many, many ways we support children's personal development in school through our Personal Development Curriculum. Click on an area in the plan to find out more.
south moreton personal development curriculum.pdf

pageCache.pageTitle: South Moreton Primary School - Unique Tech Provision
pageCache.text:
Unique Tech provision
In line with our vision to equip children with skills for a successful future, and our commitment to global citizenship, South Moreton is proud to be a Google School, educating our pupils through a unique, rich digital programme, using the Google for Education platform.
We teach high-level digital skills, computer science and coding concepts to children across the school. We use technology as a tool to expand children's digital literacy, and also to open up the world to our children by 'bringing the outside in'.
We know that tech skills will play a significant part in our pupils' futures, and they leave us with a wealth of expertise that puts them in an advantageous position for their next steps and future learning.
Children leave South Moreton being able to:
we are a google school 2 .pdf
Touch type
Collaborate digitally on presentations and documents
Code programs and hardware
Use 3D printing software and hardware
Create digital art and music
Edit media such as images and video
Research information carefully and critically
Communicate appropriately using online platforms
Act as safe, digital citizens
ESafety and Digital Citizenship
In line with our enthusiasm for digital literacy comes a commitment to ESafety and educating our children to be responsible digital citizens. We have careful filters and systems in place to ensure pupils are learning within a safe and secure digital environment.
At South Moreton we ensure our staff have up-to-date knowledge on how to ensure the safety of our pupils online. We also encourage parents and pupils to attend our ESafety sessions to ensure you can keep safe online at home.
Our ESafety policy can be found on our policies page and you can find further information at the CEOP Parent Info page.
Please do not hesitate to speak to your child's class teacher if you are worried about something your child has seen, done or experienced online.

pageCache.pageTitle: South Moreton Primary School - Extra Curricular Clubs at South Moreton
pageCache.text:
Extra Curricular Clubs at South Moreton
Children at South Moreton have the opportunity to participate in a rich variety of over 30 Extra-Curricular Clubs across the year. We structure our club provision to include a balance of sporting, craft, tech and social clubs. Activities start straight after school, with time for relaxing and eating a light tea with friends afterwards.
As part of a small local community, we also promote children's involvement in a number of local clubs and activities, with children developing a range of skills and talents across the full local offer.
Examples of clubs run over previous terms can be seen here:

Arts
STEM and cognitive skills

pageCache.pageTitle: South Moreton Primary School - Music at South Moreton
pageCache.text:
Music at South Moreton
South Moreton has a thriving musical life, with children engaged in curriculum sessions, and extra-curricular opportunities at a high level. We love music and music-making together, and we welcome families to share in this across the year.
I can see that music is really valued by the school and it shows in the way it builds the children's confidence in performance. Music really brings them to life - you can see them enjoying it, and we are really proud of them as parents too. It’s great to see that the school puts a lot of emphasis on this. (Parent feedback in Events Survey, 2025)
The Music Development Plan below outlines musical life in our school and how integral it is to our South Moreton identity.

Sport AT South Moreton
At South Moreton, we encourage children to try new activities, to perform tactically and creatively and participate to the best of their abilities. We support children to enjoy the effects of being physically active. We teach children the value of exercise for health, well being and enjoyment, alongside encouraging enthusiasm, determination and good sportsmanship.
Core PE Provision
Twice-weekly Physical Education (PE) lessons take place within the class timetable, covering the full PE curriculum. Children are taught to develop their skills within a range of sports, including creative development through gymnastics and dance.
ELITE COACHING
In addition to this, every class takes part in a full day of Elite Coaching each half term. These sessions are carefully structured, developing skills, tactics and game knowledge in the mornings, and transferring these skills into match play in the afternoons. Our Elite Coaching means we offer double the PE provision of a typical Primary School each half term, and children are well-equipped with skills across a range of competitive sports.
Extra Curricular
We run a weekly, supervised lunchtime sports club, and also a weekly after-school club, giving children the opportunity to delve deeper into skills, techniques and match play, and to push themselves further in their sport.
FACILITIES
Facilities are excellent to provide these high quality lessons, with a well equipped Sports Hall, well-marked playground and extensive playing field. Pupils also make use of our extensive grounds throughout the school day, with active learning taking place across the curriculum.
ADDITIONAL OPPORTUNITIES
We often run additional activity days and workshops which are supported by external teachers and coaches. Our most recent workshop, Capoeira, taught new skills alongside cultural understanding of the martial art.
South Moreton participates in Sports tournaments across the local area. Children in Key Stage 2 swim in the Spring and Summer Terms at a local pool.
Many of our pupils are inspired to further develop their talents in Extra-Curricular clubs provided by the school, or clubs in the local community, competing at county level.
Extra Curricular Provision
South Moreton offers a variety of extra curricular clubs, which change according to the season and to ensure a wide variety of opportunities. We run over 30 clubs per year! Examples of clubs we have run across the year are netball, football, benchball, rounders, cricket, multi-skills, archery, athletics, badminton, tennis.
You can see more about our Extra Curricular Club provision at this page.

British Values at SMS
At South Moreton, British Values are embedded within our whole-school commitment to Global Citizenship. Children learn about British Values through the acronym I Really Do Matter:
Mutual Respect and Tolerance
Children learn about British Values across the broad curriculum, within assemblies and through whole-school events e.g. making choices, signing up to their class rules and knowling those across the school, election of School Councillors, pupil survey and multicultural learning (such as Taiko drumming!)
In assemblies each week we reflect on valuable and thought-provoking questions raised through current affairs. We believe that this enables children to develop skills as thoughtful, well-informed global citizens. Each news story is grounded in British Values. An example is below, and our latest questions are available in the parent presentations part of the website and in our weekly newsletter.
We encourage parents to use the weekly assembly themes and related questions to continue the conversations at home, and to explore the themes presented in further detail. Here is an example of what we might cover in assemblies:
McDonald's is being called on to stop its introduction of paper straws in the UK, amidst claims that they dissolve in drinks. The restaurant is switching from plastic to paper straws at all of their 1,361 restaurants after customer pressure. An online petition calling for a return to plastic straws has so far gathered more than 40,000 signatures. McDonald's have said they are "doing the right thing" while some customers feel that their needs should be considered.
Things to talk about at home…
